# descriptive-link-text

- ID: `MD059`
- Category: Links and images
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `accessibility`, `links`

Link text describes its target instead of saying "click here" or "more".

## Why

Screen readers sometimes read a link without the text around it, so the link
text alone has to make sense.

## Options

Set them under `rules.descriptive-link-text.options`.

- `patterns` (`string[]`, default `[click here, here, link, more]`): Link texts
  to report, compared in any case. Also accepted as `prohibited_texts`.
- `markdownlint_compatible` (`boolean`, default `true`, gomdlint only): Compare
  link text as markdownlint does, ignoring punctuation, and skip links whose
  text holds code or HTML.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix. Only the author knows what the link should say.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

To change the options, see [here](docs/config.md).
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:29 Link text 'here' is not descriptive
```

This document follows the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

To change the options, see the [configuration guide](docs/config.md).
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  descriptive-link-text:
    options:
      patterns: [click here, here, link, more]
```

Under `rules`, `descriptive-link-text: false` turns the rule off and
`descriptive-link-text: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable descriptive-link-text` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line descriptive-link-text -->
```
